records.sourceDefinition: Roll forward a world state under hypothetical conditions to predict outcomes and compare scenarios.

sourceMetadata.name: Simulate
sourceMetadata.elevator_pitch: Roll forward a world state under hypothetical conditions to predict outcomes and compare scenarios.
sourceMetadata.example_usage: Running 'what-if' scenarios to preview system behavior before committing to a plan or action.

ux_notes.risk: False confidence from plausible-but-wrong rollouts (model mismatch, unmodeled variables, distribution shift).
ux_notes.tip: Label outputs as hypothetical, show assumptions/config used, and compare multiple scenarios rather than presenting a single future as truth.
anti_patterns: Hiding assumptions (policy, constraints, environment model) from users
Auto-executing actions directly from simulation without verification and oversight

capabilities.name: Reinforcement Learning
capabilities.example: Simulating action sequences in a control environment to estimate expected reward before acting.

capabilities.name: Robotics
capabilities.example: Previewing a robot motion plan in a simulated environment to catch collisions and failure states before execution.

capabilities.name: Time Series Forecasting
capabilities.example: Simulating multiple demand or load scenarios under different parameter assumptions (best/base/worst case).

capabilities.name: Graph Machine Learning
capabilities.example: Simulating how changes propagate through a network (e.g., supply chain disruptions spreading across dependencies).

capabilities.name: Any-to-Any
capabilities.example: Running counterfactual rollouts over mixed inputs (text + state + rules) to compare scenario outcomes.

relations.reason: Forecast predicts future values from historical series; Simulate rolls forward world state under hypothetical interventions and policies.
Planning often uses simulation to evaluate candidate action sequences ('lookahead') before choosing a plan.
Simulation results may inform actions, but should be gated by verification and human oversight in high-stakes systems.
Rollouts should be sanity-checked against constraints, historical actuals, and safety rules to reduce harmful over-trust.
Accurate rollouts depend on good initial state and parameters (often derived from estimation and sensor interpretation).

records.sourceDefinition: Discover recurring patterns from aggregate human decisions over time.

sourceMetadata.name: Harvest
sourceMetadata.elevator_pitch: Discover recurring patterns from aggregate human decisions over time.
sourceMetadata.example_usage: Identifying writing style patterns from content a user consistently accepts without editing.

ux_notes.risk: Hallucinated patterns that don't exist in source data
ux_notes.tip: Every discovered pattern must link to specific source decisions with provenance — timestamp, actor, and original context — so patterns are grounded in evidence, not AI confabulation
anti_patterns: Treating AI confidence as human validation
No verification that discovered patterns exist in source material
Patterns without provenance trail back to source decisions
Accepting pattern candidates that cannot cite concrete examples from the behavioral log

capabilities.name: Sentence Similarity
capabilities.example: Analyzing months of accepted blog posts to discover recurring phrase structures, vocabulary preferences, and formatting habits that define a writer's voice

capabilities.name: Tabular Classification
capabilities.example: Observing which product recommendations a shopper keeps versus removes over time to discover unstated preferences like avoiding synthetic fabrics

capabilities.name: Feature Extraction
capabilities.example: Mining a support team's ticket resolutions to discover that agents who include a one-line summary have 40% fewer re-opens — a pattern nobody explicitly taught

relations.reason: Harvested patterns are the input that adaptation applies. Harvest discovers what to learn; adapt updates behavior.
Individual extraction events produce raw data that harvesting aggregates into patterns over time.
Human edits — what they change and what they leave unchanged — are the primary behavioral signal.
AI-discovered patterns are prone to hallucination; verify against source material before applying.
Low-confidence patterns should be staged for human review before affecting system behavior.

Cluster groups items by similarity in a vector space at a single point in time; Harvest discovers patterns from sequential human decisions over time. Cluster is spatial (which items are near each other); Harvest is temporal (what behaviors recur across decisions). Cluster needs embeddings; Harvest needs behavioral logs with provenance.
